title: Inside the Irrigation.ltd Launch: Planning Before Hardware
excerpt: Irrigation.ltd introduces a planning-first resource for landscape watering. This private review explains its published purpose without treating navigation links as proof of operating services.
intro: Irrigation.ltd introduces itself through a question-led approach to landscape watering, rather than a catalogue of equipment. Its homepage describes practical guides spanning a first garden bed through a whole property, with planning placed before purchasing. For this private launch review, that distinction matters: the supplied homepage evidence supports an introduction to an educational resource, not a claim that contractor services, enquiry handling or other linked functions have been operationally verified.

sections.heading: A resource organised around the landscape
paragraphs: The homepage identifies home gardens, lawns and landscapes, and shared properties as its settings. It then organises the subject into drip irrigation, sprinkler systems, smarter watering, and care and troubleshooting. That structure gives the launch a clear editorial purpose: help readers understand their situation before narrowing their equipment choices.

The opening promise, “Better irrigation starts with better questions,” is therefore more than a headline to repeat. It provides a useful way to read the resource: begin with the landscape and its uncertainties, then use the relevant guidance to prepare a more informed next conversation.

sections.heading: The planning brief is the central idea
paragraphs: The most concrete planning material appears under “Before the first trench.” The homepage describes a useful project brief as a record of planting, water source, site conditions and unanswered questions. Its four-step outline asks readers to map spaces and plants; note slopes, shade, soil and existing problems; check local watering and backflow requirements; and discuss flow, pressure and design with a professional.

Those prompts establish what the proposed planning exercise is meant to cover. They do not, by themselves, demonstrate that an interactive brief builder saves information, sends a request or produces a completed design. This review treats the outline as published guidance, not evidence of those functions.

sections.heading: Different watering methods, different questions
paragraphs: The drip-irrigation introduction focuses on root-zone watering, emitters, tubing, beds and containers. The sprinkler introduction instead points to coverage, observation and questions to ask before installation. Smarter watering is framed around soil, weather and plant needs rather than a fixed habit.

These descriptions explain the site's intended comparison without establishing a universal winner. The homepage's own planning guide title—“Drip, sprinklers or hand watering: start with the plants”—reinforces that approach. For the launch, the useful distinction is between learning what needs consideration and receiving a property-specific recommendation.

sections.heading: Guide topics give the launch a practical direction
paragraphs: The homepage lists guides on choosing between watering methods, planning drip irrigation for garden beds, and watering a vegetable garden. Their descriptions introduce specific questions: landscape, soil and daily routine; emitters, filtration and root-zone coverage; and observing soil, plant stage and delivery pattern before changing a timer.

Those listings support an account of the intended editorial coverage. They are not a substitute for reviewing each full guide. The care-and-troubleshooting category similarly names leaks, uneven coverage and seasonal change as topics, without this review claiming that any particular problem has been diagnosed or resolved.

sections.heading: Attribution and enquiry boundaries
paragraphs: The footer states: “Powered by Industry Army Marketing, a division of BuildersHaus.com.” It also separates landscape-resource links from an industry-facing group that includes contractor sign-up, marketing, guest posting and business guides.

That distinction should remain explicit in launch coverage. IAM marketing enquiries are separate from a reader's irrigation-project or prospective client enquiry; the footer is not evidence that either route has been tested. This private review records the homepage's purpose, subject coverage and attribution only. It does not certify submissions, storage, delivery, contractor participation or service availability.
